_comment: Segment plan for runner.py. Segments run strictly in order; each continues from the previous one's real last frame unless marked new_scene. One plan.json per episode directory.
title: episode title, used in the stitched preview filename
scene: default scene description, used for text-to-video segments (episode openings and new_scene restarts)
cast: default cast keys for this episode, overridden per segment by in_frame

opening.image: OPTIONAL absolute path to a frame to chain the first segment from; omit for text-to-video

segments._frames: MUST satisfy the model's quantisation. MiniMax-H3: num_frames % 17 == 5 (158/175/192/209/226...362). At 24fps that is ~6.5-15s.
segments._new_scene: true restarts the chain with text-to-video. Use for a real change of time or place; a hard cut there is correct editing. Never for a cut inside one continuous conversation.
segments.scene: OPTIONAL per-segment scene override, required when new_scene is true
in_frame: keys of everyone VISIBLE in this shot
offscreen: keys of everyone present in the scene but outside the frame, including phone and voiceover speakers

beats.action: What happens, in chronological order. Counted beats beat verbs: 'takes four steps to the window, pauses, pulls the curtain in the final second' over 'walks to the window'.

beats.where: OPTIONAL position in frame, e.g. 'on the right of the frame'

beats.action: The reaction the line causes. Dialogue must sit between the action before it and the action after it, never collected into a list at the end.

segments._beats: Do NOT write a segment with no spoken line: every wordless segment generated came back with invented gibberish. Do NOT open a segment on a line: early speech gets clipped, so lead with a beat of action.
segments.text_rule: OPTIONAL override of the no-text-in-image rule, for the rare shot where a prop must legibly show text. Default forbids all writing.
